title: Types of shotgun
summary: Over-and-under, side-by-side or semi-automatic: how they differ, what the rules allow and why most shooters in Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting use an over-and-under.

body.html: Clay shooting uses a shotgun. The inside of its barrel (the bore) is smooth, with none of the spiral grooves (rifling) a rifle has. It fires a cloud of small pellets called shot, not a single bullet. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting you will meet three main types of gun.

All the guns you will see on the stand are smooth-bore shotguns. At competitions it is mostly an over-and-under (O/U): two barrels one above the other, opened by 'breaking' the gun on its hinge. Each barrel can carry its own choke, which matters for doubles.

A side-by-side has two barrels next to each other. It is the classic game gun and is allowed, but rarely seen in competition. Many shooters find that the wide top of two barrels gives the eye a less clear line, and few modern competition models are made.

A semi-automatic has one barrel and reloads itself after each shot, throwing the empty case to the side. FITASC allows it with conditions. It may hold no more than two cartridges, and its breech (the opening at the back of the barrel where the cartridge goes in) stays open whenever it is carried. In Compak® Sporting it also needs a shell catcher, so that cases do not hit the neighbour.

A semi-automatic reloads itself using either some of the gas from the shot or the kick of the recoil. Many shooters find a gas-operated one softer in the shoulder than an over-and-under, and semi-automatics often cost less.

Pump-action guns, reloaded by sliding the fore-end by hand, are not allowed in Sporting™ or in Compak® Sporting. The rulebooks state the ban without giving a reason. Compak® Sporting also bans drillings, guns that combine shotgun and rifle barrels.

Two more limits apply in both disciplines: the gauge may not be larger than 12 (so 20 gauge is fine), and barrels must be at least 66 cm long. Slings, gun-mounted cameras and any artificial aiming device are forbidden.

So why do most competition shooters use an over-and-under? First, safety: an open O/U is easy to see from a distance, so everyone knows it is empty. Second, two barrels mean two chokes: in a double the first target may be close and the second far.
Third, an over-and-under does not use the cartridge to reload, so light loads do not cause jams and no cases fly around. Finally, the narrow rib over the barrels gives the eye a clean line.

A gas-operated semi-automatic can be a good choice for a beginner or for someone who is bothered by recoil. Many shooters who stay with Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting later move to a 12-gauge competition over-and-under, a 'sporter'.

More and more grounds and some countries require steel shot. Before you buy a gun, check whether it has the steel-shot (fleur-de-lis) proof, which high performance steel loads require, and which chokes the maker allows for steel. Details: Lead, steel and soft iron and Steel shot and chokes.

notes.html: Over-and-under is one specific type of gun. Translate it with your language's word for this type, not with a general word for any double-barrelled gun.
If a client asks why pump-action guns are banned, say that it is the rule. The rulebooks give no reason, so do not invent one.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: Bring your over-and-under and a spare set of chokes.
phrases.meaning: The two-barrel competition gun plus extra choke tubes.

phrases.speaker: coach
phrases.en: With a semi-auto, keep the bolt open until you're on the stand.
phrases.meaning: Safety rule: a semi-automatic is carried with the breech open.

key_points.html: Semi-automatics are allowed: at most two cartridges, breech open when carried, shell catcher in Compak® Sporting.
Pump-action guns are banned in both disciplines; the rules give no reason.
Gauge no larger than 12, barrels at least 66 cm, no slings or aiming devices.

did_you_know.html: Many shooters set the selector so that the lower barrel of an over-and-under fires first. It sits closer to the line of the shoulder, so many people feel the gun lift a little less.

quiz.q: Which gun is NOT allowed in FITASC Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting?
quiz.explain: Pump-action guns are banned; the others are allowed if they meet the gauge and barrel limits.

quiz.q: How many cartridges may a semi-automatic hold?

options.text: As many as the magazine takes

quiz.explain: Both rulebooks limit a semi-automatic to two cartridges.

quiz.q: Why do most competition shooters choose an over-and-under?

options.text: It has the softest recoil of any type of gun
The rules allow no other type of competition gun
It is the cheapest gun that you can buy
An open O/U is easy to check and takes two chokes

quiz.explain: Visible safety, two chokes and reliability are the main reasons. Many shooters find a gas semi-automatic softer.
